stem:
Isha draws ray $OC$ from the vertex of $\angle AOB$ in the figure.

When does $OC$ bisect $\angle AOB$?

options.text: Call the answer "crease" only, without checking that the two angles at $O$ are equal.
Treat $OC$ as a bisector after checking only that it starts at $O$, skipping that $\angle AOC$ must equal $\angle COB$.
When $\angle AOC = \angle COB$, so ray $OC$ from $O$ splits $\angle AOB$ into two equal angles.
Say that equal angles $\angle AOC$ and $\angle COB$ are what create ray $OC$, instead of ray $OC$ from $O$ making those two angles.

teacher.key_rationale: An angle bisector is a ray from the vertex that splits the angle into two equal angles. Naming only "crease", dropping the equal-angle check, or reversing angles and ray all miss that hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Angle AOB with ray OC from vertex O.
